parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
When audio signals are transmitted over long distances, modulation of radio waves is used.

Suggest a reason why modulation is used.

markscheme_points.text: unmodulated (radio) waves would interfere with each other or not modulating would require aerials too long (to be practical)

hints: Hint 1: Think about the typical frequency of an audio signal and what that means for the wavelength and the practical size of a transmitting aerial, and what would happen if many stations all transmitted at those similar low frequencies.
parts.proper_answer: Audio frequencies are low so direct transmission would require impractically long aerials and signals from different stations would interfere. A high-frequency carrier is modulated to allow practical transmission.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Why audio cannot be sent directly**
Think of an audio signal of a few kHz. Its wavelength $\lambda = c/f$ is tens of kilometres, so an efficient aerial of order $\lambda/2$ would be kilometres long which is not practical. Also all audio stations occupy the same low frequency range so their waves would mix and interfere.

Step 2: **Role of modulation**
By impressing the audio information onto a high-frequency radio carrier wave of frequency e.g. $100\text{ kHz}$ to MHz, the wavelength becomes short so aerials are a few metres, and different stations can use different carrier frequencies to avoid interference.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State a technical advantage and a technical disadvantage of using frequency modulation rather than amplitude modulation.

markscheme_points.text: advantage: can transmit higher frequencies; higher quality reproduction; less prone to interference; same frequency can be used in different areas (any one point)
disadvantage: takes up greater bandwidth; shorter range of transmission; requires a greater number of transmitting aerials (any one point)

hints: Hint 1: Compare what carries the information in FM and in AM, and remember that most atmospheric and electrical noise affects amplitude but not frequency.
Hint 2: Think about the price paid for FM quality in terms of the spread of frequencies needed and how far high-frequency VHF signals travel compared to medium-wave AM signals.
parts.proper_answer: Advantage: FM gives higher quality reproduction and is less prone to interference/noise, can use higher audio frequencies. Disadvantage: FM needs greater bandwidth, has shorter range and needs more transmitting aerials.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **How FM resists noise**
In AM the information is in the amplitude, so any noise that adds to amplitude corrupts the signal. In FM the information is in the frequency and the amplitude stays constant, so amplitude noise can be removed. This gives much better quality and allows higher audio frequencies to be transmitted.

Step 2: **Cost of FM**
The frequency variation spreads the signal over a much wider band of frequencies than AM, so FM takes up greater bandwidth. FM typically uses VHF which is line-of-sight with short range, so many more transmitter aerials are needed to cover the same area.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
An audio signal of amplitude $2.0\,\mu\text{V}$ and frequency $4.2\,\text{kHz}$ is to be transmitted using a carrier wave of amplitude $10.0\,\text{mV}$ and frequency $100\,\text{kHz}$.

Either amplitude modulation or frequency modulation may be used.

The amplitude modulation is at a rate of $1\,\text{mV}\,\mu\text{V}^{-1}$.
The frequency modulation is at a rate of $5\,\text{kHz}\,\mu\text{V}^{-1}$.

Complete Table 5.1 to show the maximum and minimum values of the amplitude and of the frequency of the modulated wave for each type of modulation.

Table 5.1

markscheme_points.text: AM amplitude: min. 8 mV and max. 12 mV
AM frequency: min. 100 kHz and max. 100 kHz
FM amplitude: min. 10 mV and max. 10 mV
FM frequency: min. 90 kHz and max. 110 kHz

hints: Hint 1: Recall clearly what varies and what stays fixed: in AM the carrier frequency is unchanged but its amplitude follows the audio, in FM the amplitude is unchanged but its frequency follows the audio.
Hint 2: Use the AM rate to find how much the 10.0 mV carrier amplitude changes when the audio amplitude is 2.0 microV.
Hint 3: Use the FM rate to find how much the 100 kHz carrier frequency deviates when the audio amplitude is 2.0 microV.
Hint 4: Add and subtract each calculated variation from the carrier value to get minimum and maximum, checking units of mV and kHz.
parts.proper_answer: AM: amplitude min 8.0 mV, max 12.0 mV; frequency min 100 kHz, max 100 kHz. FM: amplitude min 10.0 mV, max 10.0 mV; frequency min 90 kHz, max 110 kHz.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Separate AM and FM behaviour**
For AM: $$\text{frequency} = \text{carrier frequency} = \text{constant}$$ and amplitude varies. For FM: $$\text{amplitude} = \text{carrier amplitude} = \text{constant}$$ and frequency varies. Here carrier is $10.0\text{ mV}$, $100\text{ kHz}$ and audio amplitude is $2.0\,\mu\text{V}$.

Step 2: **AM amplitude swing**
AM rate is $1\text{ mV}\,\mu\text{V}^{-1}$. So change in amplitude is: $$\Delta A = 1 \times 2.0 = 2.0\text{ mV}$$ Hence: $$A_{max} = 10.0 + 2.0 = 12.0\text{ mV}$$ $$A_{min} = 10.0 - 2.0 = 8.0\text{ mV}$$ Frequency stays at $100\text{ kHz}$ minimum and maximum.

Step 3: **FM frequency swing**
FM rate is $5\text{ kHz}\,\mu\text{V}^{-1}$. So frequency deviation is: $$\Delta f = 5 \times 2.0 = 10\text{ kHz}$$ Hence: $$f_{max} = 100 + 10 = 110\text{ kHz}$$ $$f_{min} = 100 - 10 = 90\text{ kHz}$$ Amplitude stays at $10.0\text{ mV}$ minimum and maximum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: For the amplitude modulated wave in **(b)**, determine the bandwidth.
hints: Hint 1: Remember that an AM wave contains the carrier plus two sidebands spaced by the audio frequency above and below the carrier, so think how wide the total spread is.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Bandwidth from sidebands**
Modulating a $100\text{ kHz}$ carrier with a $4.2\text{ kHz}$ audio signal produces side frequencies at $100 \pm 4.2\text{ kHz}$. The total width is twice the audio frequency: $$\text{bandwidth} = 2 \times f_{audio} = 2 \times 4.2 = 8.4\text{ kHz}$$
